messages:
alex.cheng: FYI customer (health-regs fintech) put a hard ask into the contract: FedRAMP-style audit bundles + signed per-tenant event export, 90-day SLA for delivery, and KMS-wrapped artifacts. Can we quickly enumerate what we currently emit and gaps?
priya.ram: Short answer: we emit tenant-scoped audit events to our internal audit pipeline and S3 exports today, but not signed bundles or per-tenant signed manifests. KMS integration exists for secrets (KMS encrypt/decrypt) but envelope signing of bundles is not implemented.
evan.kim: For clarity — current export flow = kafka -> s3 (encrypted at rest via provider-managed CMKs) -> customer download flow is via support ticket. No automated signed bundles.
marta.lopez: From compliance: customer will require tamper-evidence + verified chain-of-custody (signature + manifest + hash) and an SLA clause for delivery. Also they ask for retention proofs and redaction controls under HIPAA/BAA.
alex.cheng: @evan.kim can you paste a minimal schema for the audit events we currently emit? Need to compare fields customers expect (actor, action, resource, outcome, request_id, tenant_id, kms_key_id, timestamp).
evan.kim: Sure — current minimal event (we already have these keys):
```json
{"timestamp":"ISO8601","tenant_id":"T123","actor":"service:api","action":"model.generate","resource":"model:v1","outcome":"success","request_id":"r_abc123","meta":{}}
```
evan.kim: We do NOT include kms_key_id by default and we don't include a checksum field for bundle-level integrity.
priya.ram: Proposal: two parallel efforts — 1) schema extension to include kms_key_id, event_hash, and sequence_id; 2) signed bundle pipeline (pack events per-tenant, produce manifest with SHA256 hashes, sign with customer-wrapped KMS key).
sara.legal: Heads-up from contract side: customers want signatures from an auditable key that they can verify. They may require our signature to be verifiable against a key we publish or an attestation that the key is in an HSM. Also SLA language: "delivery within 90 days" is a long window — they likely mean monthly/quarterly bundles with 90-day turnaround for ad-hoc historical requests. We need to map time windows in the SOW.
alex.cheng: Questions for infra: can Redwood generate signatures using customer-provided public keys, or do we need to issue signed bundles with our own KMS keys and provide proof?
priya.ram: Two supported modes: A) Redwood signs with our KMS (we can provide cert/chain and key attestation), B) Redwood encrypts/signs using a customer-wrapped key (customer holds private key or wraps via KMS). Mode B is stronger for customers who don't want our signing key. Engineering complexity: B requires per-tenant keys or a secure envelope flow to avoid key proliferation.
evan.kim: Implementation notes: we can implement manifest signing in the export worker. Steps: 1) collect events per-tenant, 2) compute per-event SHA256, 3) create manifest listing filenames + hashes + sequence range, 4) sign manifest with KMS Sign API (or with private key). We'll need RBAC changes for export worker to call Sign and for ops to rotate keys safely.
marta.lopez: Also need to capture immutable event IDs and sequencing to support replay checks. Consider adding sequence_id and prev_hash to each event for tamper-evidence chains.
alex.cheng: Impact on storage/cost? Bundles + manifests + signatures will add ~5-10% extra storage and compute for hashing/signing. OK to call that out in SOW.
sara.legal: Also include retention/PD redaction clause: we should offer configurable redaction (redact PII) before packaging. Customers may require pre-redaction or full export with NDAs.
secbot: New ticket created: SEC-1347 "per-tenant signed audit bundles + manifest signing" assigned to eng-security. Link: https://tracker/internal/SEC-1347
priya.ram: Next steps: Evan to prototype manifest/sign flow and list RBAC perms needed for KMS Sign, Alex to draft contract bullet points (SLA windows, signature mode options, redaction), Marta to write required schema fields. Aim to sync in 48 hours.
evan.kim: I'll sketch a PoC branch tonight, will include sample manifest format:
```json
{"tenant_id":"T123","bundle_id":"b_20240301_01","files":[{"path":"events-0001.ndjson","sha256":"..."}],"signed_by":"redwood-kms:keys/exports/2024","signed_at":"ISO8601","signature":"BASE64"}
```
alex.cheng: Great — please include a compatibility story for existing customers (opt-in for signed bundles, a flag in console/API). We'll need console + API changes to toggle and to indicate key mode (Redwood vs Customer-wrapped).
sara.legal: I'll start draft contract language for both modes and the SLA options (monthly auto export vs ad-hoc 90-day). Pull in sales for pricing implications.
marta.lopez: I'll enumerate schema changes and a minimal validation test set for customer acceptance (sample events, manifest verification steps).
alex.cheng: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll add an item to the eng-security roadmap for Q2 and attach SEC-1347 to the sprint. :thumbsup:
